items.statement: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, including dimension zero. Let V:E→ℝ be C², α,β≥0 and η∈ℝ with α>0, α≤β, α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v∈E, η>0 and βη≤1. Fix any deterministic y,r∈E and initial phase z₀∈E×E. Put c=y−η∇V(r), Φ_t(x,p)=(c+cos(t)(x−c)+√η sin(t)p, −sin(t)(x−c)/√η+cos(t)p), g_r(x)=∇V(x)−∇V(r), S_r(x,p)=(x,p−2〈p,g_r(x)〉g_r(x)/‖g_r(x)‖²), λ_r(x,p)=√η max{0,〈p,g_r(x)〉}, Λ_z(t)=∫₀ᵗλ_r(Φ_s(z))ds and τ_z(e)=inf{t≥0:Λ_z(t)≥e}∈[0,∞], with inf empty=∞. Total real division makes S_r the identity at g_r(x)=0. The record space is D=([0,∞)×(E×E))⊕{stopped}, with Borel sum structure. Define next(e,stopped)=stopped; for a live record (T,z), next(e,(T,z))=stopped if τ_z(e)=∞, and otherwise next(e,(T,z))=(T+τ_z(e),S_rΦ_(τ_z(e))(z)). In the Lean definition untopD0 is used only in this non-top branch. Define R₀(e)=live(0,z₀) and R_(j+1)(e)=next(e_j,R_j(e)). Let Ω=ℝ^ℕ with its product Borel structure and P=⊗_(k≥0)Exp(1). Let ε(w)_k=max{w_k,0}; this is an ambient coordinate extension on a P-null nonpositive-clock set, not new source dynamics for negative clocks. For every deterministic n≥0 let H_n(w)=(R_j(ε(w)))_(0≤j≤n)∈Hist_n=D^(Fin(n+1)), and let μ_n=(H_n)_*P. Thus the last record R_n consumes only raw clocks k<n, and w_n is the next unused clock. Take any Borel function d:Hist_n→[0,∞); each d(h) is finite but the function need not be bounded. Define L(r,u,e) to mean u<τ_z(max(e,0)) when r=live(T,z), and false when r=stopped. Define q(r,u)=exp(−Λ_z(u)) when r=live(T,z), and zero when r=stopped. The event B_d={(h,v)∈Hist_n×ℝ^ℕ:L(h_n,d(h),v_0)} is Borel. The weight q_d(h)=q(h_n,d(h)) is Borel and 0≤q_d(h)≤1 for every history h. For every Borel A⊆Hist_n, P{w:H_n(w)∈A and L(R_n(ε(w)),d(H_n(w)),w_n)}=∫_A q_d(h) μ_n(dh). All conclusions hold for every deterministic y,r,z₀,n and admissible d,A under the same six standing analytic hypotheses. No positivity of μ_n(A), boundedness of d, finite-wait assumption or extra regularity/independence/conditional-law provider is required. Live histories whose next wait is infinite survive every finite d(h); stopped histories have zero weight and no fictitious phase or wait in the statement. The case n=0, null events, zero rates and dimension zero are included. Borel d and A specify admissible deterministic tests rather than additional analytic hypotheses. This is an attributed ASTIS completion of the history-dependent conditional survival ingredient implicit in AppendixA.1(A.7), using the actual recursion. Conditional finite-wait densities, ordered-time disintegration and iteration, final path factor assembly, full(A.7), physical-time residual memorylessness, random stopping/restart/Markovness, reversal, invariance, all-L² contraction, implementation error/cost, main results and actual-input composition remain separate obligations.
assumptions: E is finite-dimensional over ℝ with inner product and its Borel structure, including rank zero. V:E→ℝ is C².
The six original analytic hypotheses are α>0, α≤β, V∈C², α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v, η>0, and βη≤1; α,β≥0.
y,r,z₀ and event depth n are deterministic and universally quantified. P and the actual stopped recursion are literal definitions.
d is any Borel finite-valued nonnegative duration function of the whole finite history; A is any Borel history event. These classify test objects. d may be unbounded and μ_n(A) may vanish.

No state measurability, independence, regular conditional law, density or integrability estimate is supplied as a premise. Stopped records are guarded; live infinite waits and zero rates are permitted.
